title: The pronoun en
goal: By the end of this lesson you can use en to replace partitives, quantities and 'de + thing', keep the number in sentences like j'en ai deux, and handle en in the negative and the passé composé.

body: *En* replaces a noun introduced by a partitive or indefinite plural article: *Tu veux* **du café**? *Oui, j'***en** *veux.* (Yes, I want some.)
English often says nothing ('Yes, I want'), or 'some' / 'any'. French always needs *en*: *Tu as* **des enfants**? *Oui, j'***en** *ai.* *Non, je n'***en** *ai pas.*

head: Question
Answer with en
rows: Il y a de la neige?

learn.tip: If the noun has du, de la, de l' or des in front, the pronoun is en.

body: With a number or a quantity word, *en* replaces the noun but the quantity **stays at the end**: *J'ai* **deux** *sœurs* → *J'***en** *ai* **deux**. *Il boit* **beaucoup de** *café* → *Il* **en** *boit* **beaucoup**.
This is the part English speakers forget. 'I have two' must be *J'en ai deux*, never *J'ai deux*.

head: Full sentence
With en
rows: Je veux un kilo de pommes.

body: With verbs and expressions built with *de*, *en* replaces a thing or idea: *parler* **de** *son voyage* → *en parler*; *avoir besoin* **de** *mon auto* → *en avoir besoin*; *revenir* **de** *Toronto* → *en revenir*.
As with *y*, a **person** after *de* is not *en*: *Je parle de ma sœur* → *Je parle d'***elle**.
Same position as the other pronouns: *J'***en** *veux*. *Je n'***en** *veux pas*. *Je vais* **en** *acheter*. *J'***en** *ai acheté*.
No participle agreement with *en*: *Des pommes? J'en ai mangé* (not mangées).

With other pronouns, *en* is always last: *Il* **m'en** *a donné*. *Il* **y en** *a* (there are some). In positive commands: *Prends-***en**! *Donne-***m'en**! For *-er* verbs the *-s* comes back: *Manges-***en**!

learn.h: Il y en a, and fixed expressions
body: *Il y en a* means 'there is some / there are some': *Il reste du pain? Oui, il y en a.* Negative: *Il n'y en a pas* / *Il n'y en a plus* (there's none left).
Useful expressions: *Je m'en vais* (I'm leaving), *Je n'en peux plus* (I can't take it anymore), *Ne t'en fais pas* (don't worry), *J'en ai assez* (I've had enough).

examples.fr: Tu veux du café? Oui, j'en veux bien.
examples.en: Do you want some coffee? Yes, I'd like some.

examples.fr: Tu as des frères? J'en ai deux.
examples.en: Do you have brothers? I have two.
examples.note: the number stays at the end

examples.fr: Il y a encore de la tarte? Non, il n'y en a plus.
examples.en: Is there still some pie? No, there's none left.
examples.note: il n'y en a plus = there's no more

examples.fr: Des tomates? J'en ai acheté un kilo.
examples.note: no agreement with en in the passé composé

examples.fr: Je n'en mange jamais le matin.
examples.en: I never eat any in the morning.

examples.fr: On va en faire pour le souper.
examples.en: We're going to make some for supper.
Your trip, will you tell me about it?
examples.note: parler de + thing = en; me before en

examples.fr: J'ai besoin de ton auto. J'en ai besoin samedi.
examples.en: I need your car. I need it on Saturday.

examples.fr: Il boit trop de café. Il en boit trop.
examples.en: He drinks too much coffee. He drinks too much of it.
examples.note: quantity word stays at the end

examples.fr: Des bleuets? Prends-en, il y en a beaucoup.
examples.en: Blueberries? Take some, there are lots.
examples.note: positive command + il y en a

examples.fr: Les biscuits sont bons. Manges-en un!
examples.en: The cookies are good. Have one!

examples.fr: Je reviens de l'épicerie. J'en reviens à l'instant.
examples.en: I'm coming back from the grocery store. I've just come back from there.

examples.fr: Bon, je m'en vais. Bonne soirée!
examples.en: OK, I'm off. Have a good evening!

examples.fr: Ne t'en fais pas, ça va bien aller.
examples.en: Don't worry, it's going to be OK.

examples.fr: Combien d'heures as-tu travaillé? J'en ai travaillé dix.
examples.en: How many hours did you work? I worked ten.

quebec.intro: En is everywhere in Quebec speech, usually with 'ne' dropped and 'il y a' squeezed into 'y'a': 'j'en veux pas', 'y'en a', 'y'en a pus'. Add 'en masse' (lots, plenty), a very Quebec way of talking about quantity.

items.en: There is some / there are some.

items.note: pus = plus in casual Quebec speech
en masse = lots, plenty; Quebec, informal

items.en: I can't believe it! (I can't get over it)

drills.why: En + verb + number at the end.

drills.q: 'Je mange les pommes' (the specific apples) becomes…
drills.why: With a definite article (les), use le/la/les, not en.

drills.q: Du lait? Il n'y ___ a plus. (any)
Ton auto? J'___ ai besoin demain. (of it)
drills.en: Your car? I need it tomorrow.

drills.q: Des bonbons? Elle en veut ___. (a lot)
drills.why: The quantity stays after the verb.
Never forget en with a number.

vocab.en: some, any; of it, of them

vocab.ex: Il y en a dans le frigo.
Du pain? Il n'y en a plus.

pron.tip: [jahn-nay]: the n of en links to ai.
mahnj-ZAHN: the added s is pronounced [z].

dialogue.fr: Je vais à l'épicerie. On a besoin de lait?
dialogue.en: I'm going to the grocery store. Do we need milk?

dialogue.fr: Oui, il n'y en a plus. Prends-en deux litres.
dialogue.en: Yes, there's none left. Get two litres.

dialogue.fr: Non, y'en a en masse. J'en ai acheté une douzaine hier.
dialogue.en: No, there are plenty. I bought a dozen yesterday.

dialogue.fr: OK. Je peux acheter des bleuets aussi.
dialogue.en: OK. I can buy some blueberries too.

dialogue.fr: Bonne idée! Achètes-en beaucoup, je veux faire une tarte.
dialogue.en: Good idea! Buy lots, I want to make a pie.

dialogue.fr: Non merci, j'en bois trop ces temps-ci. Bon, vas-y, je t'en parle plus tard!
dialogue.en: No thanks, I drink too much of it these days. OK, go, we'll talk about it later!

questions.q: How much milk should A buy?
What does B want to make with the blueberries?

speak.prompt: Answer with en and a number or quantity: 'Tu as des frères et sœurs? Tu bois combien de cafés par jour? Tu as des plantes?'
speak.model: J'en ai deux: un frère et une sœur. J'en bois trois par jour. Oui, j'en ai beaucoup!

speak.prompt: You are hosting. Offer food to a guest and answer their questions using prends-en, il y en a and il n'y en a plus.
speak.model: Des biscuits? Prends-en! Il y en a beaucoup. Du vin? Désolé, il n'y en a plus.

speak.prompt: Say 'There's plenty' and 'There's none left' the standard way, then the Quebec way.
speak.model: Il y en a beaucoup. Il n'y en a plus. / Y'en a en masse. Y'en a pus.

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about what is in your fridge and what you need to buy. Use en at least five times, including with numbers and quantities.
write.model: Dans mon frigo, il y a du fromage, mais il n'y en a pas beaucoup. Des œufs? J'en ai six. Du lait? Il n'y en a plus, alors je dois en acheter. J'adore les fruits; j'en mange tous les jours. Hier, j'ai acheté des bleuets et j'en ai déjà mangé la moitié!

quiz.why: Partitive and indefinite plural articles, and de + thing.
En always comes last among the pronouns.
Y'en a pus = il n'y en a plus.

quiz.q: What does 'en masse' mean in Quebec?
quiz.why: Y'en a en masse = there's plenty.
